Exercises from Grinstead and Snell's Introduction to Probability
================================================================

This directory is a Modified Version, under the GNU Free Documentation License, of
"Grinstead and Snell's Introduction to Probability" (The CHANCE Project, version dated
22 July 2006). It contains that book's exercises only, converted for display in rika!.

Authors of the Document: Charles M. Grinstead and J. Laurie Snell; the 2006 version by
Peter G. Doyle. Modifications: Zachary Stubbs for rika! (https://github.com/ZacharySF/kitty).

Transparent copy
----------------

The source is Peter G. Doyle's official GFDL edition:

    https://math.dartmouth.edu/~doyle/docs/prob/prob.tar.gz
    SHA-256 333226cc2c2a38bb41490568e865b5769436c5f70005710280a1301039ee8577

exercises.json is generated from it, byte for byte, by scripts/extract_grinstead_snell.py
in this repository:

    uv run --locked python scripts/extract_grinstead_snell.py [--tarball prob.tar.gz] [--aux DIR]

With --aux pointing at the official build's ch1.aux ... ch12.aux (from the CHANCE copy,
https://math.dartmouth.edu/~prob/prob/), the script checks that every label it numbers
prints as in the book.


What was changed
----------------

- Only the exercises are kept: every item of every section's Exercises list, numbered as
  printed (chapter.section.number). The book's chapters, examples, figures, programs,
  appendices and index are not included, and no answers come from the book.
- The LaTeX is converted to Markdown with $...$ and $$...$$ TeX for KaTeX: references
  print their numbers; index entries and labels are dropped; enumerated parts become
  (a), (b), ...; emphasis and bold become *...* and **...**; quotes, dashes, accents and
  ties become Unicode; eqnarray becomes aligned; plain-TeX \pmatrix, \matrix and
  \bordermatrix become KaTeX matrices and ruled arrays; tables become KaTeX arrays headed
  "Table n.", with a \multicolumn cell written as its text followed by empty cells and a
  partial rule (\cline) drawn full width; footnotes are numbered with superscripts and
  placed at the end of their exercise.
- A note printed between exercises (after \medbreak) is repeated at the start of each
  exercise it introduces.
- Figures are not bundled. Exercises that refer to a figure but read without it are
  marked "figure": true.
- Exercise 11.2.27 drew a block matrix as a tabular inside display math inside \pmatrix;
  it is rewritten as the same ruled block matrix in a math array.
- Exercises left out because they can't be done without a figure that isn't bundled:
  - 4.1.32: the three road networks between Woodstock and Tunbridge are only drawn in Figure 4.6
  - 11.5.7: the maze whose transition matrix it asks for is only drawn in Figure 11.7
  - 11.5.21: the Monopoly board's squares and payoffs are only given in Figure 11.8


History
-------

- 2003: Introduction to Probability, 2nd edition, by Charles M. Grinstead and J. Laurie
  Snell, published by the American Mathematical Society.
- 2006: Grinstead and Snell's Introduction to Probability, The CHANCE Project, version
  dated 22 July 2006, by Peter G. Doyle, released under the GNU FDL.
- 2026: Exercises from Grinstead and Snell's Introduction to Probability, by Zachary
  Stubbs for rika!: the exercises extracted and converted as described above.


Not part of this Modified Version
---------------------------------

rika!'s links from these exercises to its topics, and its numeric answers to some of
them, are rika!'s own work (its own computations, not the book's), released under the
repository's MIT licence in src/kitty/core/math/textbook.py. So is the extraction script.
